pages.text: A discovery is a statistical claim. With s expected signal events over b background, the Asimov significance is Z = √(2((s+b)ln(1+s/b) − s)). Search K hypotheses at once and the look-elsewhere effect eats into it. Tight cuts keep the signal and kill the background - up to a point.
$(thing)Set$(): Exposure, Selection cut, Hypotheses tried.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Systematic drift: the signal estimate wanders by ±5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The data centre is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Less data and more parallel searches finish sooner.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Signal events: s = σ_s·L·ε_s$(br)Background events: b = σ_b·L·ε_b$(br)Local significance: Z = √(2((s+b)ln(1+s/b) − s))$(br)Global significance: Z_g² ≈ Z² − 2 ln K
